SpecFlow connects specifications, model execution, real tests, and human acceptance in one local wor

## Overview
### Traceable inputs
Each attempt records its requirements, project rules, document revisions, model, and execution ident
ity. When an upstream input changes, dependent results become stale.
### Verified candidates
Review passes examine coverage and failure cases against the same frozen materials. SpecFlow runs yo
ur project's verification commands and records their output, exit codes, and the code version tested
. Changes to code or commands invalidate old evidence.
### Explicit acceptance
Review documents, diffs, findings, and test results at each checkpoint. Before you accept a change,
SpecFlow checks that the required evidence still matches the current work.
## Get started
Choose **English** or **中文** in the workbench header. On first launch the interface follows your sys
tem or browser language; your selection is saved. The desktop menu, dialogs, status messages, and do
cument exports follow the selected interface language.
New work items use the selected language for their default workflow, generated documents, briefs, an
d clarification questions. To change the output language for a new run of an existing work item, ope
n the workflow editor and choose **Generated content language**. Existing attempts, user content, co
de, logs, and quoted evidence retain their original text. The DeepSeek Harness plugin provides the s
ame language selector within its panel.
### Desktop app
**Download the latest release**
| Platform | Installer |

| Windows x64 | `SpecFlow-<version>-win-x64.exe` |
| macOS · Apple Silicon | `SpecFlow-<version>-mac

-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS · Intel | `SpecFlow-<version>-mac-x64.dmg` |
The app includes Electron, Node.js 24, npm, and the Maka Runtime Host. Install **Git** separately, a
long with the tools your project's tests and build commands require.
**macOS validation · 2026-10-31:** A local Apple Silicon build passed native checks on macOS 27.2: 2
90 passing tests (one Windows-only check skipped), the official Maka Host, DMG/ZIP packaging, and th
e packaged CSV engineering workflow. The validation record identifies the tested revision, additiona
l desktop checks, and limits; this run covers ARM64.
Installer checksums, signing, and updates
Release assets include `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Current installers do not use Windows Authenticode or macOS
Developer ID signing; macOS builds are not notarized.
Starting with the 0.2.1 build scripts, macOS packages use complete ad-hoc signatures when Developer
ID signing and notarization are unavailable. They still require manual approval on first launch; see
the first-launch instructions. The previously published 0.2.0 macOS packages have invalid signature
s and need a new release containing this fix.
Windows supports in-place updates through the app's Help menu. For current macOS builds, download a
new DMG and replace the app. See the desktop installation and update guide.
#### Your first session
1. **Explore the demo.** The built-in CSV example changes code and runs real Node.js tests in an iso

lated repository, using deterministic results without calling a model API.
2. **Connect a repository

.** Add a local Git project with a clean, committed baseline.
3. **Configure the project.** Add a mo
del connection and choose models for the analyst, architect, developer, and reviewer roles. Set proj

ect rules and verification commands.
4. **Describe a change.** Create a work item and optionally att

ach Markdown or TXT requirements.
5. **Work through the checkpoints.** Clarify the specification, re

view and accept the design and tasks, then run implementation and verification.
6. **Accept the resu
lt.** Inspect the candidate diff, findings, and evidence before integrating into the work-item branc
.** Inspect the candidate diff, findings, and evidence before integrating into the work-item branch.
### DeepSeek Harness plugin
Run the same engineering core in a **Specflow** tab beside your DSH conversation, using the models c
onfigured in your host.
**npm · dsh-plugin-specflow 0.1.2** · GitHub release · Plugin guide
Requires **DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` or newer**, **host Node.js 24+**, and **local Git**. From `0.1.2` the pl
ugin declares the open range `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.1-rc.2"` and is verified on `0.2.1-rc.4`: DSH keep
s the plugin APIs backward compatible, so newer hosts load the same build, while older ones are stil
l skipped. The desktop app, Maka, and OpenCode are not required.
In DSH, open **Plugins → Install Third-Party Plugin** and enter `dsh-plugin-specflow@0.1.2`. Enable
it and open the Specflow workbench in the right sidebar. The panel links the current conversation's
repository automatically; you can also select a repository manually. Assign role models and verifica
tion commands, then create a work item.
For a catalog that accepts a public **npm package URL**, use https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugi
n-specflow. The GitHub release also provides a prebuilt `.tgz` and `SHA256SUMS.txt`; DSH accepts the
tarball URL or its local absolute path.
To update an installed plugin, save edits and stop active Specflow operations, uninstall it in the s
ame DSH profile, install the new package, and restart DSH. Engineering data is retained. If you conf
igured a custom `dataDir`, keep that value after reinstalling.
